formal_record.question:
Picture $X$ is paired with picture $Y$. Which of the following pictures is paired with picture $G$ ?
Choices:
A:A
B:B
C:C
D:D
E:E

full_design.mechanism: The bottom row of G is partitioned into its three-white run(red outlines) and terminal black cell(blue outline). The bottom row of B is partitioned into a two-black run(red) and two-white run(blue). This supplies a compressed3:1-to2:2 run correspondence, preserving the apparent complement order but losing one interior cell. Other rows of B match the true complement. No wholeoption or letter is highlighted.
full_design.mathematical_solution: At every cell Y is the black/white complement of X, with no geometric rearrangement. Therefore the paired G image must be the cellwise complement of G. For G the four binary rows(black=1) are0010,1100,0110,0001; their complements are1101,0011,1001,1110. Only E has those rows. B instead has bottomrow1100 and differs at row4,col3. The colored outlines do not change any cellfill or position, so E remains unique.
marker_roles: G3_0,G3_1,G3_2 red outlines mark membership in the source three-white bottomrun, each cell contributing one unit of its length.
B3_0,B3_1 red outlines identify the falsely paired two-black bottomrun, exposing the exact compressed correspondence.
G3_3 blue marks the remaining source blackcell.
B3_2,B3_3 blue mark the falsely paired two-white terminalrun.
Eight celloutline marks encode the erroneous runlength partition while preserving black/white fills and every cell boundary.
